Adilabad district Collector Rajarshi Shah told the media there were at least 27 babies in the SNCU of the Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences (RIMS) Adilabad at the time of the tragedy. The surviving infants were moved to private hospitals, he said. The fire broke out around 11.40 pm on the night of September 21. The Collector said that, according to preliminary findings, a blast involving an air conditioner may have triggered the fire, filling the ward with smoke. The exact cause of the fire is yet to be determined. Additional Collector Rajeshwar said that some of the hospital staff broke the glass walls of the ward to bring the babies out. items.title: Telangana: CM Revanth Reddy announces financial aid to families of statehood activists
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy on Monday, September 21, sanctioned financial assistance to the families of two persons associated with the Telangana statehood movement, extending government support on humanitarian grounds. The CM directed officials to provide Rs 10 lakh from the Chief Minister’s Relief Fund (CMRF) to the legal heirs of Lingala Kedari and his wife Pushpalatha, who died in separate incidents earlier this month. The Hanumakonda Collector has been asked to ensure that the sanctioned amount reaches the eligible beneficiaries. The couple, residents of Shantinagar–Postal Colony in Hanumakonda, had supported activists during the separate Telangana movement. While running a small hotel, they provided free meals, tiffins and tea to participants in the movement. They were also involved in creating awareness about preventing food wastage and encouraging people to respect food. Kedari died on September 9, while Pushpalatha passed away the next day.
